the Tibet hybrid experiment has been used to study the energy spectrum of CRs and its chemical composition.
the Tibet hybrid data cannot be explained in a simple way by diffusive shock acceleration in supernova remnants.

the knee feature of CRs can be interpreted in terms of the diffusive acceleration at SNRs and the sharp knee observed by the Tibet experiment suggests that the nearby sources contribute to the observed knee feature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of CR origin by combining the results of the Tibet experiment with those of the KASCADE experiment.
the study of the origin of the knee in the cosmic-ray energy spectrum and its possible connection with the chemical composition.
the origin of CRs in the energy range of 10^14-10^17 eV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the origin of the knee is not yet understood.
the knee of the cosmic ray spectrum is not yet fully understood.
the knee in the spectrum of CR nuclei is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple diffusive shock acceleration picture is not enough to explain the observed data.
the origin of the knee could be explained by both the diffusion and the acceleration processes at nearby SNRs.
the diffusive shock mechanism can be used to describe the origin of the knee in CR spectrum and that the knee in CR composition can be interpreted in the same way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical composition of CRs around the knee is consistent with the prediction of the diffusive acceleration theory.
the knee in CR spectrum could be explained by a combination of nearby sources and diffusive shock acceleration.
the knee is not a universal feature of CRs.
